Stratify curation output by curator

Source: R/curation_handling.R
stratifyByCurator.Rd

Counts the number of signatures and papers each person contributed to. Columns such as "Revision editor" can list several people per signature (e.g. "Claregrieve1,Chloe,WikiWorks743"); these entries are split so that each person is credited individually, regardless of their position in the list.

Usage

stratifyByCurator(
  dat,
  col = "Curator",
  sep = ",",
  exclude = "^WikiWorks",
  short.names = TRUE
)

Arguments

dat

a data.frame storing BugSigDB data

col

character. The column of dat listing the people to count. Defaults to "Curator"; use "Revision editor" to count revision contributions.

sep

character. Separator between multiple people in col.

exclude

character. A regular expression; people whose name matches it are dropped. Defaults to dropping the WikiWorks maintenance accounts. Use NULL to keep everyone.

short.names

logical. Shorten names to the first word for display (e.g. "Aleru Divine" becomes "Aleru")? Names whose first word is shared by more than one person are kept in full.

Value

a numeric matrix with rows "signatures" and "papers" and one column per person, ordered by increasing number of papers.

Examples

dat <- data.frame(PMID = c(1, 1, 2, 3),
                  `Revision editor` = c("Ann,WikiWorks743", "Ann,Bob",
                                        "Bob", "WikiWorks"),
                  check.names = FALSE)
stratifyByCurator(dat, col = "Revision editor")
#>            Ann Bob
#> signatures   2   2
#> papers       1   2
